October 2026

8 October · Christopher Waller · The Signaling Value of the Summary of Economic Projections

Waller argued that the Fed could signal the likely direction and extent of tightening while retaining flexibility on timing. After September’s quarter-point increase to 3.75–4.00%, he saw a stable labour market and inadequate progress on inflation. He cited August core PCE at 3% year over year and expected further increases if the economy evolved as forecast. The three-hike example illustrates the communication framework. His account of the September projections and fed funds futures indicates that further tightening was already expected by many participants and market traders, though their horizons differed.

Questions for further research. 1. Did the speech change pricing for a particular meeting? Compare timestamped fed funds futures before and after publication. 2. Which inflation releases could change the inferred pace of tightening? Compare subsequent releases with the inflation assumptions discussed in the speech. 3. How much does the dispersion of the September dots matter? Compare individual dots across horizons and examine how the market priced those horizons.

November 2026

10 November · Michelle Bowman · The U.S. Economy and Considerations for Monetary Policy

Bowman supported the October hold at 3.75–4.00% while stressing persistent inflation and a more stable labour market. Low hiring alongside low layoffs made that stability fragile. She inferred from the CPI release that October core PCE inflation likely reached 3.3% year over year. Her forecast for inflation to approach target in 2027 depended partly on tariffs, energy and AI-related price pressures easing. She described AI investment as a source of near-term demand and capacity pressure with potential longer-term productivity benefits. Increased external financing also creates a downside channel if revenues disappoint and valuations fall. She noted that higher private borrowing costs and wider spreads had already tightened financial conditions somewhat.

Questions for further research. 1. Is inflation broadening beyond the categories Bowman highlights? Check PCE component contributions and inflation expectations. 2. Is low hiring beginning to translate into rising layoffs? Compare claims and job-finding rates. 3. How much do rising spreads threaten AI investment and adjacent borrowers? Review financing disclosures and compare issuer spreads. For an event study, verify the first public release time and account for the CPI release on the same date.
